title: AlignDefTok: Training-Free Transfer of DefensiveTokens via Embedding-Space Alignment

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to eliminate the ~16 GPU-hour per-model training cost of DefensiveTokens prompt-injection defenses. None of the prior papers explicitly address the same objective of reducing the computational cost of training DefensiveTokens defenses. While several papers (e.g., [4], [8], [13]) discuss prompt injection defenses, their focus is on improving security or robustness, not on reducing the training cost of a specific defense mechanism like DefensiveTokens. Therefore, no prior paper shares this purpose.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, AlignDefTok, transfers DefensiveTokens between related models (same tokenizer and embedding dimension) to enable defense reuse without retraining. This mechanism is a form of transfer learning or parameter-efficient adaptation. Papers like [19], [23], and [27] discuss soft prompt transfer or prompt tuning for cross-task or cross-lingual transfer, which are substantively equivalent mechanisms. For example, [23] introduces Soft Prompt Transfer (SPoT), which transfers learned prompts between tasks, and [19] discusses multitask prompt tuning for efficient transfer learning. These mechanisms align with the underlying primitive of transferring learned parameters (or embeddings) across related models or tasks.

### Evaluation
The evaluation demonstrates 133-285x compute savings versus full DefensiveTokens training while matching native defense performance (0-1.9% ASR on AlpacaFarm). Papers like [4] and [13] evaluate prompt injection defenses using similar designs, such as measuring attack success rates (ASR) and comparing defense performance. While the specific benchmark (AlpacaFarm) and compute savings metric are new, the evaluation design — comparing defense effectiveness and efficiency — is not novel. For example, [4] evaluates DefensiveTokens by measuring ASR, and [13] evaluates defense combinations by comparing their effectiveness. Thus, the evaluation design is covered.

### Domain
The domain is LLM security, specifically prompt injection defense. Many prior papers, including [4], [8], [13], and [15], operate in this domain. For example, [4] focuses on DefensiveTokens for prompt injection defense, and [8] discusses defenses against prompt injection attacks in LLMs. Therefore, the domain is covered.
